# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1212
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1212
- **Title**: gh-1204 [BUG] main red: Terminal visual leg — /approval picker renders nothing after #1143 (tool-misuse breaker) merged at bbec345
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1204` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +127
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-10-03T21:51:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T13:21:34Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

- The red leg was a **torn-frame snapshot race**, not a `/approval` defect. The CI failure screen shows the `[Approval mode]` title row painted with **zero item rows** — impossible in a committed frame (`_writeMenu` paints title + items from one atomic model state), so the test's 50 ms poll read a partially applied frame.
- The cell-diff renderer emits frame rows as incremental writes; the harness's hosted `xterm` emulator does not answer the DEC 2026 DECRQM probe, so frames are never atomic there. Under arm-CI load the CLI stalled mid-frame (the screen also carried the still-settling submit's `Working… 0s · submit` row and a stale duplicate fold-hint row — two frames interleaved).
- #1143's merge correlation is coincidental: its diff never touches the composer → `/approval` → `openPicker` path, and the **same commit passed the same leg 32 minutes later** (run 37146775783).

### Fix

- `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness.dart`: `liveWaitForScreen` gains an opt-in `settle` gate — after the first screen match, hold until the raw byte stream goes quiet (bounded 2 s grace so spinner streams can't hang), re-check the pattern, and return the settled screen. Torn frames can no longer satisfy a settled wait.
- `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/fa_cli_visual_test.dart`: the `/approval` picker wait uses `settle: true`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`: picker items extracted behind `approvalPickerItemsForTest()` (mirrors `settingsHubItemsForTest`), no behavior change.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/approval_cli_test.dart` (ticket direction b, fast core lane): `always-ask mode is the single (current) row` + `/approval <mode> moves the (current) marker` — pins the picker contract without a PTY so a genuine regression fails pre-merge.
- `flutter test test/cli_visual`: **50 passed, 4 skipped** (fixture-gated omp skips, same as CI) — includes the fixed approval test, also verified green under an 8-way CPU load.
- Full core suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **8671 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- bbec345 was verified green-on-rerun upstream; no revert needed (fix direction (a) found no throw/no-op to fix forward — the handler was always correct).
- Two pre-existing environment issues in this sandbox, both reproduced identically on pristine bbec345 and unrelated to the change: `tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts with native heap corruption (pty2/VM on this runner), and `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` needs `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`/`FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` unset (this runner exports them).
- The omp parity tests keep the legacy (unsettled) wait path by default — settle is opt-in, so mid-run streaming waits are unchanged.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1212
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1212
- **Title**: gh-1204 [BUG] main red: Terminal visual leg — /approval picker renders nothing after #1143 (tool-misuse breaker) merged at bbec345
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1204` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 97
- **Additions**: +115
- **Deletions**: -3
- **Created**: 2026-10-03T21:51:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-03T22:41:30Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

- The red leg was a **torn-frame snapshot race**, not a `/approval` defect. The CI failure screen shows the `[Approval mode]` title row painted with **zero item rows** — impossible in a committed frame (`_writeMenu` paints title + items from one atomic model state), so the test's 50 ms poll read a partially applied frame.
- The cell-diff renderer emits frame rows as incremental writes; the harness's hosted `xterm` emulator does not answer the DEC 2026 DECRQM probe, so frames are never atomic there. Under arm-CI load the CLI stalled mid-frame (the screen also carried the still-settling submit's `Working… 0s · submit` row and a stale duplicate fold-hint row — two frames interleaved).
- #1143's merge correlation is coincidental: its diff never touches the composer → `/approval` → `openPicker` path, and the **same commit passed the same leg 32 minutes later** (run 37146775783).

### Fix

- `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness.dart`: `liveWaitForScreen` gains an opt-in `settle` gate — after the first screen match, hold until the raw byte stream goes quiet (bounded 2 s grace so spinner streams can't hang), re-check the pattern, and return the settled screen. Torn frames can no longer satisfy a settled wait.
- `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/fa_cli_visual_test.dart`: the `/approval` picker wait uses `settle: true`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`: picker items extracted behind `approvalPickerItemsForTest()` (mirrors `settingsHubItemsForTest`), no behavior change.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/approval_cli_test.dart` (ticket direction b, fast core lane): `always-ask mode is the single (current) row` + `/approval <mode> moves the (current) marker` — pins the picker contract without a PTY so a genuine regression fails pre-merge.
- `flutter test test/cli_visual`: **50 passed, 4 skipped** (fixture-gated omp skips, same as CI) — includes the fixed approval test, also verified green under an 8-way CPU load.
- Full core suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **8671 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- bbec345 was verified green-on-rerun upstream; no revert needed (fix direction (a) found no throw/no-op to fix forward — the handler was always correct).
- Two pre-existing environment issues in this sandbox, both reproduced identically on pristine bbec345 and unrelated to the change: `tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts with native heap corruption (pty2/VM on this runner), and `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` needs `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`/`FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` unset (this runner exports them).
- The omp parity tests keep the legacy (unsettled) wait path by default — settle is opt-in, so mid-run streaming waits are unchanged.

# gh-1204: [BUG] main red: Terminal visual leg — /approval picker renders nothing after #1143 (tool-misuse breaker) merged at bbec345

## Description

**Symptom**: ci.yml on main @ bbec345 (run 37144742018, 2026-10-03 18:35Z) fails the Terminal visual (PTY screenshots) leg: `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/fa_cli_visual_test.dart: always-ask mode → approval mode set → /approval shows mode` — Expected: contains '(current)'; Actual screen shows the echoed `/approval` and «21 lines above fold» — the picker output NEVER rendered.

**Regression window**: main was green at 4c92c4f (18:15Z); bbec345 = merge of #1143 (feat #862 tool-misuse resilience) is the only delta → red at 18:41Z. The ec3637e red/green pair was a DIFFERENT flake (PTY/CLI integration shard 2/3), so this visual failure is new, not the known flake.

**Suspect mechanism**: #1143 touched `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`, `agent_cli_config.dart`, `agent_cli.dart` (ToolMisuseBreaker wiring, `beginRun()` in `_runAgentLoop`). The `/approval` output vanishing smells like the command path now throws or no-ops under the new config field (e.g. breaker config parse breaking the slash-command handler, or a config-object shape change breaking the approval command's state read). Verify: run the visual test locally on bbec345, then on 4c92c4f — must be green there.

**Fix directions**: (a) find the throw/no-op in the /approval handler under the post-#1143 config shape and fix forward; (b) add a unit test asserting `/approval` output contains '(current)' in always-ask mode (the visual test caught it — a cheap CLI unit test would have caught it pre-merge); (c) if the root cause slips, revert bbec345 to green main and re-land #1143 with the test.

**Note**: #1143 spent days in the red park with validation_failed; its gate went green on a rerun — check whether the visual leg actually ran on its final head (guest-content gate failures may have masked this leg).

Tracker: #1167 (ci-red). Supersedes nothing; closes when main goes green with this test passing.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1212
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1212
- **Title**: gh-1204 [BUG] main red: Terminal visual leg — /approval picker renders nothing after #1143 (tool-misuse breaker) merged at bbec345
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1204` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +127
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-10-03T21:51:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T13:21:34Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

- The red leg was a **torn-frame snapshot race**, not a `/approval` defect. The CI failure screen shows the `[Approval mode]` title row painted with **zero item rows** — impossible in a committed frame (`_writeMenu` paints title + items from one atomic model state), so the test's 50 ms poll read a partially applied frame.
- The cell-diff renderer emits frame rows as incremental writes; the harness's hosted `xterm` emulator does not answer the DEC 2026 DECRQM probe, so frames are never atomic there. Under arm-CI load the CLI stalled mid-frame (the screen also carried the still-settling submit's `Working… 0s · submit` row and a stale duplicate fold-hint row — two frames interleaved).
- #1143's merge correlation is coincidental: its diff never touches the composer → `/approval` → `openPicker` path, and the **same commit passed the same leg 32 minutes later** (run 37146775783).

### Fix

- `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness.dart`: `liveWaitForScreen` gains an opt-in `settle` gate — after the first screen match, hold until the raw byte stream goes quiet (bounded 2 s grace so spinner streams can't hang), re-check the pattern, and return the settled screen. Torn frames can no longer satisfy a settled wait.
- `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/fa_cli_visual_test.dart`: the `/approval` picker wait uses `settle: true`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`: picker items extracted behind `approvalPickerItemsForTest()` (mirrors `settingsHubItemsForTest`), no behavior change.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/approval_cli_test.dart` (ticket direction b, fast core lane): `always-ask mode is the single (current) row` + `/approval <mode> moves the (current) marker` — pins the picker contract without a PTY so a genuine regression fails pre-merge.
- `flutter test test/cli_visual`: **50 passed, 4 skipped** (fixture-gated omp skips, same as CI) — includes the fixed approval test, also verified green under an 8-way CPU load.
- Full core suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **8671 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- bbec345 was verified green-on-rerun upstream; no revert needed (fix direction (a) found no throw/no-op to fix forward — the handler was always correct).
- Two pre-existing environment issues in this sandbox, both reproduced identically on pristine bbec345 and unrelated to the change: `tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts with native heap corruption (pty2/VM on this runner), and `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` needs `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`/`FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` unset (this runner exports them).
- The omp parity tests keep the legacy (unsettled) wait path by default — settle is opt-in, so mid-run streaming waits are unchanged.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes

  user asks "what do you know about X".

  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,

If the marker never moves (regression), `marked` would be `[always-ask row]`... wait no, second test starts with `write` mode and switches to yolo. If the regression is "marker not moved", `marked.single` = 'write' row → expect fails with a clear diff. If the regression is "no marker at all", `marked.single` throws StateError "No element" — less friendly but still a failure. Minor.

Wait, there's one more consideration for the second test: `cli.approvalPickerItemsForTest()` reads `_approval.mode`. Does `/approval yolo` in LINE MODE (not TUI) update `_approval.mode`? The existing test above confirms `cli.approval.mode` becomes yolo — and `_approval` presumably is that same approval manager. Let me check agent_cli.dart `_approval`.

Also — in TUI mode the visual test sends `/approval` and the picker opens. In line mode (isInteractive, supportsRawMode false), `/approval` prints the mode list. The unit test's `/approval yolo` goes through the slash-command handler. Good.

Now, is there potential flake: `_waitFor` polls for 'approval mode set to yolo' in output — fine, matches existing test patterns.

Now the deeper question — the ROOT CAUSE analysis. The PR claims the CI failure was a torn-frame snapshot race, NOT a real regression from #1143. Is this plausible and does the fix address it? The claim: the harness's xterm emulator doesn't answer DECRQM, so frames are applied incrementally as bytes stream; under load the 50ms poll caught the title row painted but item rows not yet. Plausible. The fix: settle gate + unit test pinning the contract. This is fix direction (b)-ish from the ticket plus a harness hardening; ticket direction (a) concluded no defect exists.

Hmm, but wait — there's a subtle question about the test change. The original failure: "Expected: contains '(current)'; Actual screen shows the echoed `/approval`". With settle:true, after `[Approval mode]` appears, wait for raw-quiet (400ms min), re-check pattern, then the test asserts `screenText` contains 'always-ask' and '(current)'. One residual gap: the assertions after `liveWaitForScreen` read `harness.screenText` directly rather than the returned settled screen. Between the return and the two expect calls, `screenText` getter is called twice — each reads current buffer state. In theory the screen could change between the settled return and the asserts (e.g. a fold-hint repaint) — but since the stream went quiet, practically fine. This is also consistent with the rest of the file's style. Not worth flagging? Could be a small suggestion: assert on the returned screen instead of re-reading `harness.screenText` twice. Actually, `expect(harness.screenText, ...)` twice = two separate reads; the returned value IS available. Minor consistency nit — the method returns the settled screen for a reason. I'd fold this into a suggestion.

Bigger potential issue in the settle loop: consider the scenario where the pattern appears on screen at time T, and raw output keeps streaming for >2s (grace expires, returns false), settled screen still contains pattern → return settled. That's the documented fallback. OK.

Now consider: pattern appears, settle runs, pattern VANISHED while settling (transient), loop continues, 50ms later pattern back, settle again 400ms min... each loop iteration with a transient match costs ≥450ms. With 15s timeout that's ~30 iterations. Fine.

And what about `waitForRawSettle` being called even when the frame is already complete — i.e., the common green-path cost: every settled wait now costs ≥600ms (3 turns × 200ms: first iteration always records lastLength, then two stable turns). Actually: iteration 1: delay 200ms, lastLength -1 → != raw → set lastLength, stableTurns 0. Iteration 2: delay 200ms, equal → stableTurns 1. Iteration 3: delay 200ms, equal → stableTurns 2 → return true. So ~600ms per settled wait, plus the initial match. Acceptable for a 15s-timeout visual test. Fine.

Another thing to check: `waitForRawSettle`'s grace deadline starts BEFORE the first delay; with default grace 2s and settleMs 200 → at most 9-10 iterations. OK.

buffer instead. That reopens a (narrow) window for exactly the tear the gate closes: each getter
call re-reads the live buffer, so the two asserts can even straddle a repaint and disagree.

```dart
final settled = await harness.liveWaitForScreen(
  '[Approval mode]',
  timeout: const Duration(seconds: 15),
  settle: true,
);
expect(settled, contains('always-ask'));
expect(settled, contains('(current)'));
```

Practically low-risk (the raw stream just went quiet for 400 ms+), but the returned value exists for
this purpose — pinning it costs nothing and makes the fix airtight.

- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T13:21:34Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

- The red leg was a **torn-frame snapshot race**, not a `/approval` defect. The CI failure screen shows the `[Approval mode]` title row painted with **zero item rows** — impossible in a committed frame (`_writeMenu` paints title + items from one atomic model state), so the test's 50 ms poll read a partially applied frame.
- The cell-diff renderer emits frame rows as incremental writes; the harness's hosted `xterm` emulator does not answer the DEC 2026 DECRQM probe, so frames are never atomic there. Under arm-CI load the CLI stalled mid-frame (the screen also carried the still-settling submit's `Working… 0s · submit` row and a stale duplicate fold-hint row — two frames interleaved).
- #1143's merge correlation is coincidental: its diff never touches the composer → `/approval` → `openPicker` path, and the **same commit passed the same leg 32 minutes later** (run 37146775783).

### Fix

- `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness.dart`: `liveWaitForScreen` gains an opt-in `settle` gate — after the first screen match, hold until the raw byte stream goes quiet (bounded 2 s grace so spinner streams can't hang), re-check the pattern, and return the settled screen. Torn frames can no longer satisfy a settled wait.
- `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/fa_cli_visual_test.dart`: the `/approval` picker wait uses `settle: true`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`: picker items extracted behind `approvalPickerItemsForTest()` (mirrors `settingsHubItemsForTest`), no behavior change.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/approval_cli_test.dart` (ticket direction b, fast core lane): `always-ask mode is the single (current) row` + `/approval <mode> moves the (current) marker` — pins the picker contract without a PTY so a genuine regression fails pre-merge.
- `flutter test test/cli_visual`: **50 passed, 4 skipped** (fixture-gated omp skips, same as CI) — includes the fixed approval test, also verified green under an 8-way CPU load.
- Full core suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **8671 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- bbec345 was verified green-on-rerun upstream; no revert needed (fix direction (a) found no throw/no-op to fix forward — the handler was always correct).
- Two pre-existing environment issues in this sandbox, both reproduced identically on pristine bbec345 and unrelated to the change: `tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts with native heap corruption (pty2/VM on this runner), and `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` needs `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`/`FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` unset (this runner exports them).
- The omp parity tests keep the legacy (unsettled) wait path by default — settle is opt-in, so mid-run streaming waits are unchanged.

`waitForRawSettle` (lines 375–392) re-implements, verbatim, the stability loop of `waitForOutput`
(lines ~401–415): `deadline` from a Duration, `lastLength = -1`, `stableTurns`, poll every
`settleMs`, return/break after 2 stable turns. The doc comment even has to say "Same stability rule

This code exists to fight flakes; a future tweak to the stability rule (3 turns, different
`settleMs`, trimming `_rawBuffer` so `.length` is not monotonic) must now land in two places, and
missing one silently reintroduces the torn-frame race this PR fixes. Extract one private core, e.g.:

```dart
/// True when no new raw bytes arrived for [settleMs] twice in a row before
/// [deadline] (bounded by it).
Future<bool> _rawQuiet(int settleMs, DateTime deadline) async {
  var lastLength = -1;
  var stableTurns = 0;
  while (DateTime.now().isBefore(deadline)) {
    await Future<void>.delayed(Duration(milliseconds: settleMs));
    if (_rawBuffer.length == lastLength) {
      if (++stableTurns >= 2) return true;
    } else {
      stableTurns = 0;
      lastLength = _rawBuffer.length;
    }
  }
  return false;
}
```

Then `waitForOutput` becomes `await _rawQuiet(settleMs, DateTime.now().add(timeout)); return
_rawBuffer.toString();` and `waitForRawSettle` is a 2-line wrapper.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1212
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1212
- **Title**: gh-1204 [BUG] main red: Terminal visual leg — /approval picker renders nothing after #1143 (tool-misuse breaker) merged at bbec345
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1204` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 97
- **Additions**: +115
- **Deletions**: -3
- **Created**: 2026-10-03T21:51:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-03T22:41:30Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

- The red leg was a **torn-frame snapshot race**, not a `/approval` defect. The CI failure screen shows the `[Approval mode]` title row painted with **zero item rows** — impossible in a committed frame (`_writeMenu` paints title + items from one atomic model state), so the test's 50 ms poll read a partially applied frame.
- The cell-diff renderer emits frame rows as incremental writes; the harness's hosted `xterm` emulator does not answer the DEC 2026 DECRQM probe, so frames are never atomic there. Under arm-CI load the CLI stalled mid-frame (the screen also carried the still-settling submit's `Working… 0s · submit` row and a stale duplicate fold-hint row — two frames interleaved).
- #1143's merge correlation is coincidental: its diff never touches the composer → `/approval` → `openPicker` path, and the **same commit passed the same leg 32 minutes later** (run 37146775783).

### Fix

- `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness.dart`: `liveWaitForScreen` gains an opt-in `settle` gate — after the first screen match, hold until the raw byte stream goes quiet (bounded 2 s grace so spinner streams can't hang), re-check the pattern, and return the settled screen. Torn frames can no longer satisfy a settled wait.
- `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/fa_cli_visual_test.dart`: the `/approval` picker wait uses `settle: true`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`: picker items extracted behind `approvalPickerItemsForTest()` (mirrors `settingsHubItemsForTest`), no behavior change.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/approval_cli_test.dart` (ticket direction b, fast core lane): `always-ask mode is the single (current) row` + `/approval <mode> moves the (current) marker` — pins the picker contract without a PTY so a genuine regression fails pre-merge.
- `flutter test test/cli_visual`: **50 passed, 4 skipped** (fixture-gated omp skips, same as CI) — includes the fixed approval test, also verified green under an 8-way CPU load.
- Full core suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **8671 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- bbec345 was verified green-on-rerun upstream; no revert needed (fix direction (a) found no throw/no-op to fix forward — the handler was always correct).
- Two pre-existing environment issues in this sandbox, both reproduced identically on pristine bbec345 and unrelated to the change: `tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts with native heap corruption (pty2/VM on this runner), and `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` needs `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`/`FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` unset (this runner exports them).
- The omp parity tests keep the legacy (unsettled) wait path by default — settle is opt-in, so mid-run streaming waits are unchanged.

# gh-1204: [BUG] main red: Terminal visual leg — /approval picker renders nothing after #1143 (tool-misuse breaker) merged at bbec345

## Description

**Symptom**: ci.yml on main @ bbec345 (run 37144742018, 2026-10-03 18:35Z) fails the Terminal visual (PTY screenshots) leg: `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/fa_cli_visual_test.dart: always-ask mode → approval mode set → /approval shows mode` — Expected: contains '(current)'; Actual screen shows the echoed `/approval` and «21 lines above fold» — the picker output NEVER rendered.

**Regression window**: main was green at 4c92c4f (18:15Z); bbec345 = merge of #1143 (feat #862 tool-misuse resilience) is the only delta → red at 18:41Z. The ec3637e red/green pair was a DIFFERENT flake (PTY/CLI integration shard 2/3), so this visual failure is new, not the known flake.

**Suspect mechanism**: #1143 touched `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`, `agent_cli_config.dart`, `agent_cli.dart` (ToolMisuseBreaker wiring, `beginRun()` in `_runAgentLoop`). The `/approval` output vanishing smells like the command path now throws or no-ops under the new config field (e.g. breaker config parse breaking the slash-command handler, or a config-object shape change breaking the approval command's state read). Verify: run the visual test locally on bbec345, then on 4c92c4f — must be green there.

**Fix directions**: (a) find the throw/no-op in the /approval handler under the post-#1143 config shape and fix forward; (b) add a unit test asserting `/approval` output contains '(current)' in always-ask mode (the visual test caught it — a cheap CLI unit test would have caught it pre-merge); (c) if the root cause slips, revert bbec345 to green main and re-land #1143 with the test.

**Note**: #1143 spent days in the red park with validation_failed; its gate went green on a rerun — check whether the visual leg actually ran on its final head (guest-content gate failures may have masked this leg).

Tracker: #1167 (ci-red). Supersedes nothing; closes when main goes green with this test passing.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

Under arm-CI load the CLI stalled mid-frame (the screen also carried the still-settling submit's `Working… 0s · submit` row and a stale duplicate fold-hint row — two frames interleaved).

- `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness.dart`: `liveWaitForScreen` gains an opt-in `settle` gate — after the first screen match, hold until the raw byte stream goes quiet (bounded 2 s grace so spinner streams can't hang), re-check the pattern, and return the settled screen. Torn frames can no longer satisfy a settled wait.
- `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/fa_cli_visual_test.dart`: the `/approval` picker wait uses `settle: true`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`: picker items extracted behind `approvalPickerItemsForTest()` (mirrors `settingsHubItemsForTest`), no behavior change.

- `test/cli/approval_cli_test.dart` (ticket direction b, fast core lane): `always-ask mode is the single (current) row` + `/approval <mode> moves the (current) marker` — pins the picker contract without a PTY so a genuine regression fails pre-merge.
- `flutter test test/cli_visual`: **50 passed, 4 skipped** (fixture-gated omp skips, same as CI) — includes the fixed approval test, also verified green under an 8-way CPU load.
- Full core suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **8671 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- bbec345 was verified green-on-rerun upstream; no revert needed (fix direction (a) found no throw/no-op to fix forward — the handler was always correct).
- Two pre-existing environment issues in this sandbox, both reproduced identically on pristine bbec345 and unrelated to the change: `tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts with native heap corruption (pty2/VM on this runner), and `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` needs `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`/`FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` unset (this runner exports them).

# SM kicker — a tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost).
#
# Canonical home for the SM-kicker watchdog every factory repo points at.
# The calling repo keeps a thin stub workflow that calls this one with the
# repo-specific names (defaults match flutter_agent_harness).
#
# Why it exists: a repo whose CI is dispatch-only (no `on.push` on PR
# heads) and whose Machine SM is the sole trigger has two gaps that leave
# a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet strict
#      `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on the new
#      head SHA. Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents,
#      0 files vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check
#      contexts NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on it.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).

name: Factory SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the Machine SM workflow in the caller repo'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'Workflow display NAME as it appears in the runs API'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check context names'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'SM workflow file'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'CI workflow file to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'CI workflow display name'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check contexts'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

permissions:
  actions: write        # workflow_dispatch: sm / ci
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # Global group, but NO cancel-in-progress (fa #911 diagnosis,
  # 2026-09-25): a push on ANY PR branch used to kill the in-flight kicker
  # for every other branch, leaving sm-liveness/head-completeness
  # check-runs stamped CANCELLED on random heads and polluting PR check
  # rolls repo-wide. The kicker jobs are seconds-cheap watchdogs — let
  # them queue instead of cancelling; a bounded backlog is harmless.
  group: factory-sm-kicker
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
  SM_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.sm_workflow || 'machine-sm.yml' }}
  CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow || 'ci.yml' }}
  CI_DISPLAY: ${{ inputs.ci_display_name || 'CI' }}
  REQUIRED_CONTEXTS: ${{ inputs.required_contexts || 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate' }}

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/$SM_WORKFLOW/runs?per_page=1" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending")] | length')
          if [ "${active:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "SM alive ($active active run(s)) — nothing to do"
          else
            echo "SM idle — dispatching a tick"
            # Real tick, always: the workflow_dispatch default is dryRun=true
            # (a safety default for HUMAN dispatches). A bare dispatch from the
            # kicker lands dry and cannot merge anything — live evidence
            # 2026-10-03: dart kicker fired within 7s of #340's checks but the
            # SM ran "(dry)" (runs 37152253853, 37157212391); every merge that
            # night rode manual -F dryRun=false ticks instead.
            gh workflow run "$SM_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" -F dryRun=false
          fi

  head-completeness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch CI on codeless PR heads that carry no required contexts
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != "branch" ]; then echo "tag push — skip"; exit 0; fi
            branches=("${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
          else
            mapfile -t branches < <(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName')
            echo "scanning ${#branches[@]} open PR branch(es)"
          fi
          IFS=',' read -ra contexts <<< "$REQUIRED_CONTEXTS"
          jq_ctx=$(printf '%s\n' "${contexts[@]}" | jq -R . | jq -s .)
          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }
            read -r parents files < <(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha" --jq '"\(.parents | length) \(.files | length)"')

            if [ "${found:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: ${sha:0:9} already has required contexts — skip"
              continue
            fi

            sleep 45

- **Title**: gh-1204 [BUG] main red: Terminal visual leg — /approval picker renders nothing after #1143 (tool-misuse breaker) merged at bbec345
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1204` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 97
- **Additions**: +115
- **Deletions**: -3
- **Created**: 2026-10-03T21:51:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-03T22:41:30Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

- The red leg was a **torn-frame snapshot race**, not a `/approval` defect. The CI failure screen shows the `[Approval mode]` title row painted with **zero item rows** — impossible in a committed frame (`_writeMenu` paints title + items from one atomic model state), so the test's 50 ms poll read a partially applied frame.
- The cell-diff renderer emits frame rows as incremental writes; the harness's hosted `xterm` emulator does not answer the DEC 2026 DECRQM probe, so frames are never atomic there. Under arm-CI load the CLI stalled mid-frame (the screen also carried the still-settling submit's `Working… 0s · submit` row and a stale duplicate fold-hint row — two frames interleaved).
- #1143's merge correlation is coincidental: its diff never touches the composer → `/approval` → `openPicker` path, and the **same commit passed the same leg 32 minutes later** (run 37146775783).

### Fix

- `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness.dart`: `liveWaitForScreen` gains an opt-in `settle` gate — after the first screen match, hold until the raw byte stream goes quiet (bounded 2 s grace so spinner streams can't hang), re-check the pattern, and return the settled screen. Torn frames can no longer satisfy a settled wait.
- `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/fa_cli_visual_test.dart`: the `/approval` picker wait uses `settle: true`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`: picker items extracted behind `approvalPickerItemsForTest()` (mirrors `settingsHubItemsForTest`), no behavior change.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/approval_cli_test.dart` (ticket direction b, fast core lane): `always-ask mode is the single (current) row` + `/approval <mode> moves the (current) marker` — pins the picker contract without a PTY so a genuine regression fails pre-merge.
- `flutter test test/cli_visual`: **50 passed, 4 skipped** (fixture-gated omp skips, same as CI) — includes the fixed approval test, also verified green under an 8-way CPU load.
- Full core suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **8671 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- bbec345 was verified green-on-rerun upstream; no revert needed (fix direction (a) found no throw/no-op to fix forward — the handler was always correct).
- Two pre-existing environment issues in this sandbox, both reproduced identically on pristine bbec345 and unrelated to the change: `tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts with native heap corruption (pty2/VM on this runner), and `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` needs `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`/`FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` unset (this runner exports them).
- The omp parity tests keep the legacy (unsettled) wait path by default — settle is opt-in, so mid-run streaming waits are unchanged.

## Description

**Symptom**: ci.yml on main @ bbec345 (run 37144742018, 2026-10-03 18:35Z) fails the Terminal visual (PTY screenshots) leg: `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/fa_cli_visual_test.dart: always-ask mode → approval mode set → /approval shows mode` — Expected: contains '(current)'; Actual screen shows the echoed `/approval` and «21 lines above fold» — the picker output NEVER rendered.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Now, is there potential flake: `_waitFor` polls for 'approval mode set to yolo' in output — fine, matches existing test patterns.

Now the deeper question — the ROOT CAUSE analysis. The PR claims the CI failure was a torn-frame snapshot race, NOT a real regression from #1143. Is this plausible and does the fix address it? The claim: the harness's xterm emulator doesn't answer DECRQM, so frames are applied incrementally as bytes stream; under load the 50ms poll caught the title row painted but item rows not yet. Plausible. The fix: settle gate + unit test pinning the contract. This is fix direction (b)-ish from the ticket plus a harness hardening; ticket direction (a) concluded no defect exists.

Hmm, but wait — there's a subtle question about the test change. The original failure: "Expected: contains '(current)'; Actual screen shows the echoed `/approval`". With settle:true, after `[Approval mode]` appears, wait for raw-quiet (400ms min), re-check pattern, then the test asserts `screenText` contains 'always-ask' and '(current)'. One residual gap: the assertions after `liveWaitForScreen` read `harness.screenText` directly rather than the returned settled screen. Between the return and the two expect calls, `screenText` getter is called twice — each reads current buffer state. In theory the screen could change between the settled return and the asserts (e.g. a fold-hint repaint) — but since the stream went quiet, practically fine. This is also consistent with the rest of the file's style. Not worth flagging? Could be a small suggestion: assert on the returned screen instead of re-reading `harness.screenText` twice. Bigger potential issue in the settle loop: consider the scenario where the pattern appears on screen at time T, and raw output keeps streaming for >2s (grace expires, returns false), settled screen still contains pattern → return settled. That's the documented fallback. OK.

Now consider: pattern appears, settle runs, pattern VANISHED while settling (transient), loop continues, 50ms later pattern back, settle again 400ms min... each loop iteration with a transient match costs ≥450ms. With 15s timeout that's ~30 iterations. Fine.

And what about `waitForRawSettle` being called even when the frame is already complete — i.e., the common green-path cost: every settled wait now costs ≥600ms (3 turns × 200ms: first iteration always records lastLength, then two stable turns). Actually: iteration 1: delay 200ms, lastLength -1 → != raw → set lastLength, stableTurns 0. Iteration 2: delay 200ms, equal → stableTurns 1. Iteration 3: delay 200ms, equal → stableTurns 2 → return true. So ~600ms per settled wait, plus the initial match. Acceptable for a 15s-timeout visual test. Fine.

Another thing to check: `waitForRawSettle`'s grace deadline starts BEFORE the first delay; with default grace 2s and settleMs 200 → at most 9-10 iterations. OK.

- **PR #**: 1212

- **Title**: gh-1204 [BUG] main red: Terminal visual leg — /approval picker renders nothing after #1143 (tool-misuse breaker) merged at bbec345
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1204` → `main`
- **State**: open

- **Additions**: +127
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-10-03T21:51:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T13:21:34Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

- The red leg was a **torn-frame snapshot race**, not a `/approval` defect. The CI failure screen shows the `[Approval mode]` title row painted with **zero item rows** — impossible in a committed frame (`_writeMenu` paints title + items from one atomic model state), so the test's 50 ms poll read a partially applied frame.
- The cell-diff renderer emits frame rows as incremental writes; the harness's hosted `xterm` emulator does not answer the DEC 2026 DECRQM probe, so frames are never atomic there. Under arm-CI load the CLI stalled mid-frame (the screen also carried the still-settling submit's `Working… 0s · submit` row and a stale duplicate fold-hint row — two frames interleaved).
- #1143's merge correlation is coincidental: its diff never touches the composer → `/approval` → `openPicker` path, and the **same commit passed the same leg 32 minutes later** (run 37146775783).

### Fix

- `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness.dart`: `liveWaitForScreen` gains an opt-in `settle` gate — after the first screen match, hold until the raw byte stream goes quiet (bounded 2 s grace so spinner streams can't hang), re-check the pattern, and return the settled screen. Torn frames can no longer satisfy a settled wait.
- `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/fa_cli_visual_test.dart`: the `/approval` picker wait uses `settle: true`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`: picker items extracted behind `approvalPickerItemsForTest()` (mirrors `settingsHubItemsForTest`), no behavior change.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/approval_cli_test.dart` (ticket direction b, fast core lane): `always-ask mode is the single (current) row` + `/approval <mode> moves the (current) marker` — pins the picker contract without a PTY so a genuine regression fails pre-merge.
- `flutter test test/cli_visual`: **50 passed, 4 skipped** (fixture-gated omp skips, same as CI) — includes the fixed approval test, also verified green under an 8-way CPU load.
- Full core suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **8671 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- bbec345 was verified green-on-rerun upstream; no revert needed (fix direction (a) found no throw/no-op to fix forward — the handler was always correct).
- Two pre-existing environment issues in this sandbox, both reproduced identically on pristine bbec345 and unrelated to the change: `tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts with native heap corruption (pty2/VM on this runner), and `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` needs `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`/`FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` unset (this runner exports them).
- The omp parity tests keep the legacy (unsettled) wait path by default — settle is opt-in, so mid-run streaming waits are unchanged.

blocks.text:
# SM kicker — a tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost).
#
# Canonical home for the SM-kicker watchdog every factory repo points at.
# The calling repo keeps a thin stub workflow that calls this one with the
# repo-specific names (defaults match flutter_agent_harness).
#
# Why it exists: a repo whose CI is dispatch-only (no `on.push` on PR
# heads) and whose Machine SM is the sole trigger has two gaps that leave
# a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet strict
#      `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on the new
#      head SHA. Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents,
#      0 files vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check
#      contexts NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on it.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).

name: Factory SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the Machine SM workflow in the caller repo'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'Workflow display NAME as it appears in the runs API'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check context names'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'SM workflow file'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'CI workflow file to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'CI workflow display name'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check contexts'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

permissions:
  actions: write        # workflow_dispatch: sm / ci
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # Global group, but NO cancel-in-progress (fa #911 diagnosis,
  # 2026-09-25): a push on ANY PR branch used to kill the in-flight kicker
  # for every other branch, leaving sm-liveness/head-completeness
  # check-runs stamped CANCELLED on random heads and polluting PR check
  # rolls repo-wide. The kicker jobs are seconds-cheap watchdogs — let
  # them queue instead of cancelling; a bounded backlog is harmless.
  group: factory-sm-kicker
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
  SM_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.sm_workflow || 'machine-sm.yml' }}
  CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow || 'ci.yml' }}
  CI_DISPLAY: ${{ inputs.ci_display_name || 'CI' }}
  REQUIRED_CONTEXTS: ${{ inputs.required_contexts || 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate' }}

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/$SM_WORKFLOW/runs?per_page=1" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending")] | length')
          if [ "${active:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "SM alive ($active active run(s)) — nothing to do"
          else
            echo "SM idle — dispatching a tick"
            # Real tick, always: the workflow_dispatch default is dryRun=true
            # (a safety default for HUMAN dispatches). A bare dispatch from the
            # kicker lands dry and cannot merge anything — live evidence
            # 2026-10-03: dart kicker fired within 7s of #340's checks but the
            # SM ran "(dry)" (runs 37152253853, 37157212391); every merge that
            # night rode manual -F dryRun=false ticks instead.
            gh workflow run "$SM_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" -F dryRun=false
          fi

  head-completeness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch CI on codeless PR heads that carry no required contexts
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != "branch" ]; then echo "tag push — skip"; exit 0; fi
            branches=("${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
          else
            mapfile -t branches < <(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName')
            echo "scanning ${#branches[@]} open PR branch(es)"
          fi
          IFS=',' read -ra contexts <<< "$REQUIRED_CONTEXTS"
          jq_ctx=$(printf '%s\n' "${contexts[@]}" | jq -R . | jq -s .)
          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }
            read -r parents files < <(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha" --jq '"\(.parents | length) \(.files | length)"')
            if [ "$parents" != "2" ] || [ "${files:-1}" != "0" ]; then
              echo "$b: code-bearing head — SM owns validation, skip"
              continue
            fi
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq --arg name "$CI_DISPLAY" '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == $name and (.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending"))] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI already active on ${sha:0:9} — skip"
              continue
            fi
            found=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" \
              --jq --argjson ctx "$jq_ctx" '[.check_runs[].name | select(. as $n | $ctx | index($n))] | length')
            if [ "${found:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: ${sha:0:9} already has required contexts — skip"
              continue
            fi
            # grace re-check: a CI dispatch may be in flight from the SM/chain
            sleep 45
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq --arg name "$CI_DISPLAY" '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == $name)] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI appeared during grace window — skip"
              continue
            fi
            echo "$b: codeless head ${sha:0:9} with zero required contexts — dispatching CI"
            gh workflow run "$CI_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref "$b"
          done

Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1212
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1212
- **Title**: gh-1204 [BUG] main red: Terminal visual leg — /approval picker renders nothing after #1143 (tool-misuse breaker) merged at bbec345
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1204` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 97
- **Additions**: +115
- **Deletions**: -3
- **Created**: 2026-10-03T21:51:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-03T22:41:30Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

- The red leg was a **torn-frame snapshot race**, not a `/approval` defect. The CI failure screen shows the `[Approval mode]` title row painted with **zero item rows** — impossible in a committed frame (`_writeMenu` paints title + items from one atomic model state), so the test's 50 ms poll read a partially applied frame.
- The cell-diff renderer emits frame rows as incremental writes; the harness's hosted `xterm` emulator does not answer the DEC 2026 DECRQM probe, so frames are never atomic there. Under arm-CI load the CLI stalled mid-frame (the screen also carried the still-settling submit's `Working… 0s · submit` row and a stale duplicate fold-hint row — two frames interleaved).
- #1143's merge correlation is coincidental: its diff never touches the composer → `/approval` → `openPicker` path, and the **same commit passed the same leg 32 minutes later** (run 37146775783).

### Fix

- `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/cli_visual_harness.dart`: `liveWaitForScreen` gains an opt-in `settle` gate — after the first screen match, hold until the raw byte stream goes quiet (bounded 2 s grace so spinner streams can't hang), re-check the pattern, and return the settled screen. Torn frames can no longer satisfy a settled wait.
- `flutter_app/test/cli_visual/fa_cli_visual_test.dart`: the `/approval` picker wait uses `settle: true`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`: picker items extracted behind `approvalPickerItemsForTest()` (mirrors `settingsHubItemsForTest`), no behavior change.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/approval_cli_test.dart` (ticket direction b, fast core lane): `always-ask mode is the single (current) row` + `/approval <mode> moves the (current) marker` — pins the picker contract without a PTY so a genuine regression fails pre-merge.
- `flutter test test/cli_visual`: **50 passed, 4 skipped** (fixture-gated omp skips, same as CI) — includes the fixed approval test, also verified green under an 8-way CPU load.
- Full core suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **8671 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- bbec345 was verified green-on-rerun upstream; no revert needed (fix direction (a) found no throw/no-op to fix forward — the handler was always correct).
- Two pre-existing environment issues in this sandbox, both reproduced identically on pristine bbec345 and unrelated to the change: `tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts with native heap corruption (pty2/VM on this runner), and `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` needs `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`/`FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` unset (this runner exports them).
- The omp parity tests keep the legacy (unsettled) wait path by default — settle is opt-in, so mid-run streaming waits are unchanged.
